key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface electrostatics more uniform and more stable under light, indicating reduced grain-boundary barriers and lower electronic disorder.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane passivation can improve perovskite solar-cell voltage stability and reduce photovoltage losses by creating a more homogeneous carrier landscape.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to map dark CPD and illuminated SPV
Compare passivated vs. unpassivated mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior contributions and probe wavelength-dependent SPV
evidence_signal: AEAPTMS narrowed the dark CPD distribution from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the SPV stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The results come from thin-film nanoscale measurements, so device-level performance gains still need verification under full solar-cell operating conditions.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
